title: Where Did Time Disappear When You Were Young?
core_idea: The activities that made you forget time as a child may hold quiet clues about what still nourishes your soul, not as a career plan but as a thread worth following.
text: Think back to when you were small. What made the hours vanish? Maybe it was drawing, or building forts, or asking endless questions about the stars. Nobody paid you for it. Nobody praised it as a calling. You simply forgot the clock. Many people find that those early absorptions leave a faint trace that never fully disappears. It doesn't have to become a job or a grand plan. But perhaps it is worth asking what that child already knew. What was it about the drawing, the building, the wondering, that felt so right? Follow that feeling a little today, even for ten minutes. It may still know the way.
description: A gentle reflection on how the things that made you forget time as a child may still hold quiet clues about your purpose.
